screens: Forgot password → after 'Request recovery' · 1440 (and phones without mobile Access) · EN + ES
shot: Not captured. Read from code. Start state: pub-forgot-en-1440.png.
what: After sending, the title still says 'Forgot password' and the subtitle still says 'We’ll email you a recovery link.' A card appears with 'Request received' and one hedged sentence. No envelope mark, no 'check spam', no mention that the link expires in 15 minutes, no way to resend or correct a typo, no 'Back to sign in'. 'I have a recovery code' and 'Can’t use your email?' stay on screen as if nothing happened. The phone variant behind the flag already does this well ('Check your email', envelope, expiry).
why: Peak-end rule and feedback. A 15-minute link that nobody is told about produces 'this link can’t be used' ten minutes later, and the person blames the product.

It works once and expires in 15 minutes. Check spam too.' / ES 'Si el ID de empleado y el correo coinciden con una cuenta, te enviamos un enlace. Funciona una sola vez y vence en 15 minutos. Revisa también el correo no deseado.' Actions: primary 'Back to sign in' / 'Volver a iniciar sesión'; text link 'Didn’t get it? Check your details' / '¿No llegó? Revisa tus datos' (reopens the form with the values kept). Hide the 'I have a code' pill in this state.

screens: Session expired → Sign in · all widths
shot: Not captured. Read from code. The person sees pub-signin-*.png with nothing added.
what: When a session ends, the app redirects to a bare /login: no message, and no return address. The person is mid-task (approving a timecard, reading a pay statement), the screen silently becomes 'Good morning', and after signing in they land on Home, not where they were.
why: Visibility of system status and trust. A payroll product that drops you without a word reads as a crash or as being hacked.
fix: Redirect to /login?reason=expired&returnTo={path} (returnTo is already supported and vetted). Show a calm teal information note above the fields, not red: EN 'You were signed out to keep your account safe. Sign in to pick up where you left off.' / ES 'Cerramos tu sesión para proteger tu cuenta. Inicia sesión para continuar donde estabas.'

screens: Help someone sign in (manager) → New password (employee) · all widths
shot: Not captured (signed-in page). Read from code. Employee side: pub-reset-en-390.png.
what: A manager who verifies someone in person gets a 43-character random code in a read-only field with a 'Select' button and the instruction 'Share it privately'. The employee must then open Forgot password, tap 'I have a recovery code' and enter those 43 characters. There is no copy button, no link, no QR code. The guidance also says not to use a new email or phone, so the realistic channel is reading it aloud or a personal chat app.
why: Effort and error rate at the exact moment someone is locked out before a shift. It also pushes the secret into uncontrolled channels.
fix: On the manager’s receipt show a QR code (220px, white card) that opens /reset-access#proof=… on the employee’s own phone, with 'Copy link' as the primary button and the raw code behind 'Show code'. Copy: EN 'Have them scan this with their phone camera. It works once, until {time}.' / ES 'Pídele que lo escanee con la cámara de su teléfono. Funciona una sola vez, hasta las {time}.' The employee then lands on New password with the code already applied.

screens: Spanish sign-in → first screen in the app · all widths · ES
what: The six sign-in pages are fully Spanish. The moment a Spanish-speaking person signs in, the product is English ('3 things need you', 'Things to do'). The employee getting-started guide is called with lang="en" hard-coded. The file comment says 'Only these four pages switch; the rest of the app stays English.'
why: Broken promise at the hand-off. A Spanish front door implies a Spanish product; the cliff is felt as 'this isn’t really for me'.
fix: Until the app is translated, set the expectation on the sign-in page in Spanish only, as a 13px grey line under the card: ES 'Por ahora, la aplicación está en inglés después de iniciar sesión.' Pass the chosen language into the employee guide. Put app translation (Employee Home, Schedule, Time, Pay first) on the roadmap as the real fix.

screens: Bare domain / · all widths
shot: No capture of /. It ends at pub-signin-*.png.
what: / redirects to /app, which redirects signed-out people to /login: two hops and no page of its own. A company owner who types the domain, or anyone who is sent the link, sees a sign-in form with no description of what NEVORA is, who it is for, or how to get an account. There is no self-serve sign-up, so the only way in is an invitation.
why: First impression. Sign-in-first is the norm for an app subdomain (app.gusto.com, workforcenow.adp.com, app.joinhomebase.com), but those products also have a marketing site on the main domain. NEVORA has neither, so the sign-in page has to carry the introduction.
fix: See the landing recommendation in review-public.md. Minimum: redirect / straight to /login when there is no session cookie (one hop), and make the sign-in page a proper front door (PB-011, PB-012).

screens: Forgot password · 390 + 1440 · EN + ES
what: Three stacked actions: filled 'Request recovery', an outlined pill of the same size 'I have a recovery code', and a text disclosure 'Can’t use your email?'. On desktop the secondary pill is inside the card, 12px under the primary, and competes with it. On the phone the same pill sits outside the card. The 'not yet' mark is a minus-in-circle, which reads as 'remove' or 'blocked'. One line ends in a full stop and the other does not ('At least 8 characters.' / 'Passwords match'). screens: Invitation and reset emails

Body EN 'Hi {first name}, {Company} uses NEVORA for schedules, hours and pay. Set up your account to see yours. This link works once and expires in 7 days.' Button 'Set up my account'. ES 'Hola, {nombre}: {Company} usa NEVORA para horarios, horas y pago. Configura tu cuenta para ver los tuyos. Este enlace funciona una sola vez y vence en 7 días.' Botón 'Configurar mi cuenta'. shot: Not captured (off in this environment). Read from code.
what: The passkey button is a grey words-only pill under Sign in with no icon and no divider. Its error is a plain red paragraph without the icon the other alerts have. The Face ID glyph in the file is a hand-drawn SVG, not Phosphor, and is unused in this variant.
why: Consistency of alerts and icons; the faster option should be recognisable at a glance.
fix: Outlined pill, 48px, with Phosphor bold 20px 'Fingerprint' (computers) or 'ScanSmiley' (phones) before the label, 12px under Sign in after a centred 13px 'or' / 'o'. Error uses the standard alert (WarningCircle bold 20px + text).

what: The language pill is 36px tall with a 4px invisible extension (44px hit area); the back link is 44px. The design system asks for 48px targets. On sub-pages the back link starts 22px from the top of the screen.
why: Brand rule (48px) and comfortable reach under a phone’s status area.
fix: Make both hit areas 48px (pseudo-element inset -6px on the pill). Give the phone band 16px above the first row plus the safe-area inset.

why: Proximity: a group label belongs 12px above its group and 32px below the previous one.

screens: Privacy, Terms · 390 vs 1440
shot: pub-privacy-en-390.png vs pub-privacy-en-1440.png; pub-terms-en-390.png vs pub-terms-en-1440.png
what: On desktop every section is open and still shows a collapse caret; on phones every section is closed, so the policy opens as a list of twelve headings with no text. The desktop contents list omits 'Questions'.
why: A policy should be readable without twelve taps; a control that is rarely useful is clutter.
fix: Phones: open the first section by default and add 'Open all' / 'Abrir todo' at the top. Desktop: remove the carets (plain headings) since the contents list already navigates. Add 'Questions' to the contents list.

what: The card is 812px wide for one sentence and a small button at the left. 'Powered by VELANI LLC' and '© 2026 VELANI LLC' are stacked. 'Error 404' sits under the title as a subtitle.
why: Proportion and redundancy; low stakes.
fix: Cap the card at 560px and centre it; keep one VELANI line. Fine to leave 'Error 404'.

screens: Sign in · first paint
what: The server sends 'Welcome back' and the page swaps to 'Good morning' after it loads, so the title changes under the reader. A new hire arriving from activation is also told 'Welcome back'.
why: No text changing after paint; register for a first-time visitor.
fix: After activation (?activated=1) use 'Welcome' / 'Te damos la bienvenida'. Reserve the title’s height and fade the swap over 120ms, or render the greeting only on the client with the space held.

screens: All auth forms · phones
what: Fields don’t set the keyboard’s action key. Email correctly uses the email keyboard; Employee ID uses the default keyboard with capitals off (right if IDs can contain letters).
why: Mobile-native feel: the keyboard’s key should say Next, then Go.
fix: enterKeyHint="next" on every field except the last, "go" on the last. Add autoCorrect="off" to Employee ID and the reset code. If Employee IDs are digits only, add inputMode="numeric".
